THE MIXINS WRITE STATE THEY CANNOT DECLARE, AND THAT IS THE WHOLE SHAPE OF IT.
`BaseModel` is assembled from a dozen mixins that all inherit `_ModelStubs`, and
the slots, the fields and half the methods live on classes the mixin cannot see.
Three mechanisms cover most of the 135:

  1. `_ModelStubs.__slots__` is declared in the TYPE_CHECKING branch now, beside
     the attributes it describes. The runtime tuple is still empty and
     `BaseModel.__slots__` still owns the storage; what changed is that mypy can
     see WHERE `env`, `_ids` and `_prefetch_ids` live, so six assignments in
     `IterationMixin` and two in `_DisplayNameMixin` stop reading as writes to
     names no slot holds.
  2. Fourteen members that exist at runtime and were declared nowhere:
     `__setitem__`, `__sub__`, `__contains__`, `__int__`, `mapped`, `grouped`,
     `fields_get`, `invalidate_model`, `update_field_translations`,
     `_read_format`, `_fetch_query`, `_is_an_ordinary_table`, `_write_multi`,
     `_update_cache`, `_order_to_sql`, `_traverse_related_sql`, `_transient`.
     Every one was an unchecked call through the mixin surface.
  3. `resolve_fnames`, `Field._insert_cache`, `Field._clear_dead_pending`,
     `_get_stored_translations` and `Registry.is_an_ordinary_table` take
     `ModelLike` -- the alias this repository already has for "a recordset or a
     mixin standing in for one" -- rather than `BaseModel`. That is what they
     accept; it is now what they say.

`Environment.user` is `ResUsersProtocol`, and `decimal.precision`,
`ir.model.fields.selection` and `ir.model.relation` join `_protocols.py` with
their `__getitem__` overloads. `test_framework_contracts` checks every declared
member against the real model, so none of it can drift.

FOUR NARROWINGS WITH A RAISING ACCESSOR, same shape as the previous change:
`Properties._get_definition_record`, `Many2many._get_relation_triple` (reused by
`model_test_env`), `Selection._get_selection`, and the `read_group` granularity
and definition-record paths.

SEVEN SHADOWED LOCALS were the other recurring cause -- one name bound to two
types in one scope, which mypy reports at the second binding and a reader never
sees at all: `ids` in `_RelationalMulti.convert_to_cache` (a tuple, then an
OrderedSet), `fields` in `load()` (str paths, then tuples), `record` in
`_load_records`, `granularity` in `_read_group_orderby`, `value` in
`_value_to_date`, `fill_from`/`fill_to` in `_read_group_fill_temporal`, `cls` in
`ModelRegistry`. Each is now two names.

THREE OF MY OWN REGRESSIONS WERE CAUGHT BY THE INTEGRATION SUITE and are
recorded because none was visible to `pytest odoo/orm/tests`:
  - `copy_data` filtered out its `None` slots to satisfy a return type. Those
    slots keep the list aligned with `self` and `copy()` zips them strict --
    11 `test_translate` failures. The annotation is `list[ValuesType | None]`
    now, which is what the method has always returned.
  - `_export_rows` wrote `f"{model},{id}"` where the xmlid PAIR belongs -- 4
    failures in `test_export_import_roundtrip`.
  - importing `Granularity` from `odoo.libs.datetime.date_utils` instead of the
    `odoo.libs.datetime` facade failed `libs_facade_check` in Tier 1.
The lesson is the one this branch keeps relearning: a type error is a question
about the code, and the answer is not always the annotation.
